# Review CHANGES REQUESTED for PAN-4358

# Review — PAN-4358
## Verdict: CHANGES REQUESTED — per-root conversation lookups over the 300-chunk pool block the dashboard event loop ~250–500 ms per palette search (NFR-1 budget ~50 ms)

## Context
- Run ID: agent-pan-4358-review-66aaf3fa
- Manifest: /home/eltmon/Projects/overdeck/workspaces/feature-pan-4358/.pan/review/agent-pan-4358-review-66aaf3fa/context.json
- Branch / workspace: feature/pan-4358 / /home/eltmon/Projects/overdeck/workspaces/feature-pan-4358
- PR: https://github.com/eltmon/overdeck/pull/4375
- HEAD reviewed: 66aaf3faf40ed1cb336622421e4c3b5c6cb5a112
- Base / prior cycle SHA: merge-base 76fba679f85 (origin/main); no prior review cycle

## Blocking Findings

### [performance] Resolving 300 chunk hits runs up to ~250–450 full-scan SQLite lookups synchronously on the dashboard server — `src/dashboard/server/routes/palette.ts:361`
- Severity: ! (fails explicit in-scope NFR-1; material event-loop blocking)
- Classification / requirement scope: implementation defect, in_pr_scope. The PRD's WI-4 prescribed `resolve: (root) => toIdentity(routeableConversation(root, cache))` (per-root memoized lookup), so the spec design contributes; NFR-1 ("Grouping and classification of a 300-chunk pool add no more than ~50 ms") is the requirement it breaks. Spec correction: WI-4 should resolve all distinct roots in one batched query.
- Trigger and changed-code connection: `searchConversations()` now asks `searchConversationChunks()` for `CONVERSATION_CHUNK_POOL = 300` fused hits (was `limit` = 15 from the palette). `groupConversationHits()` calls `resolve(root)` for each hit; the memoized `routeableConversation()` calls `getConversationByClaudeSessionId()` once per **distinct root session**. That function (`src/lib/overdeck/conversations.ts:640`) runs `WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM conversation_files cf WHERE cf.conversation_id = c.id AND cf.locator = ?)`; `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` on the live DB is `SCAN c` + `SEARCH cf USING INDEX conv_files_conv_idx (conversation_id=?)` — there is no index on `cf.locator`, so every miss scans all 3157 conversation rows. Chunk sessions for agents/specialists/unregistered Claude sessions mostly have no conversation row, so misses dominate.
- Expected / observed / impact: expected ≤~50 ms added (NFR-1). Observed, running the same WHERE clause with better-sqlite3 read-only against the live `~/.overdeck/overdeck.db` over the distinct roots of the real BM25 top-300 from the live `embeddings.db`:
  - `eltmon`: 255 roots, 71 with a conversation row → 310 ms
  - `review`: 152 roots, 102 with a row → 237 ms
  - `deploy`: 125 roots, 8 with a row → 268 ms
  - `portfolio`: 15 roots → 33 ms
  - a miss costs ~1.6 ms (300 misses: 494 ms); a hit ~0.2 ms.
  The vector top-300 adds its own distinct roots, so real totals are higher (estimated 0.3–0.6 s). Baseline made ≤15 lookups (~25 ms). All of this is synchronous better-sqlite3 work on the dashboard server, so every HTTP request, WebSocket frame and poll stalls for that time after each 120 ms-debounced keystroke in Ctrl+K (`useDebouncedValue(query, 120)`, `CommandPalette.tsx:341`); a client-side abort does not stop the server work.
- Evidence: read-only probe scripts (better-sqlite3, `readonly: true`) against the live DBs; query plan above. Limits: probe used `SELECT c.*` rather than `LEGACY_CONVERSATION_SELECT` (same WHERE clause and plan, so the column list does not change the scan cost); vector-pool roots were not measured, so the numbers are a lower bound. The title search itself is cheap (0.8–3.5 ms).
- Fix: before calling `groupConversationHits()`, collect the distinct root session ids of `hits` and resolve them with one query, e.g.
  `SELECT cf.locator, c.name, c.project_key, c.title, c.archived_at FROM conversation_files cf JOIN conversations c ON c.id = cf.conversation_id WHERE cf.locator IN (…)` (chunked to SQLite's parameter limit), pre-filling the `routeableConversations` cache (misses → `{ name: root, projectKey: null, title: null, archived: false }`). That is one scan of `conversation_files` (~5k rows, ~1–2 ms) instead of hundreds of scans of `conversations`. Put the batch helper in a new module (not `conversations.ts`, which is at its file-size cap). Add a palette test asserting one batched lookup regardless of hit count, and amend WI-4 in the PRD accordingly.

## Non-blocking Findings

- ~ **[requirements] PR's frontend tests are not run by CI** — `package.json` `test:frontend-subset` is an explicit file list; `palette-conversation-hits.test.ts` (new), `CommandPalette.test.tsx` and `App/api.test.ts` are not in it, and `vitest.config.ts` excludes `src/dashboard/frontend/**`. FR-7/FR-8/FR-9 evidence therefore relies on local runs only. Add the three files to `test:frontend-subset`. (Pre-existing pattern for the two older files; the new file is this PR's.)
- ~ **[correctness] Misleading source chip for titled conversations with no Claude session** — `palette.ts` title-only branch sets `sessionId = titleMatch.sessionId ?? identity.conversationId`. For a conversation with no `claude-code` file (codex/pi/etc.), `describeConversationHit()` sees `conversationId === rootSessionId`, so `isDashboardConversation` is false and the chip reads `Claude session 20260919` (first 8 chars of the conversation name). Opening still works (`App.tsx:498` uses `conversationId` first). Fix: treat title-only rows (`byteOffset === null`) as dashboard conversations, or compare against a null session id.
- ~ **[correctness] Non-ASCII uppercase letters in titles miss the SQL prefilter** — `conversation-title-search.ts` uses `lower(c.title) LIKE ?`; SQLite folds ASCII only, while `queryTerms()` lowercases with Unicode rules. A title like "ÉTUDE…" never reaches `titleMatchesQuery` for query `étude`. Rare; could drop `lower()`-based prefiltering for non-ASCII terms or do the fold in JS over a broader prefilter.
- ≉ **[correctness] CodeRabbit: stale target on a reused pane (`App.tsx:543`)** — traced: `AgentPane.onTargetMessageHandled` clears `targetMessageId/Index/Nonce` once applied, and the subagent effect is keyed on the nonce. The residual case is a target not yet applied when the same conversation is reopened through a title-only row. Clearing the target fields in the title-only `updatePane` call is a cheap hardening; not a demonstrated defect.
- ? **[correctness] FR-6 when `getHandle()` throws** — `searchConversationChunks()` calls `getHandle()` synchronously; a throw would reject `Promise.all` in `searchConversations()` and drop title matches. `createConversationEmbeddingProvider()` returns unavailable providers instead of throwing and `openEmbeddingsDb()` wraps its open in try/catch, so no reachable throw was found. A test with a throwing handle would establish impact.
- Spec note (not a finding): issue AC1 says a title match returns "the first conversation result". With several title matches only one can be first; on live data "portfolio" matches two titles and the newer one ("Portfolio tablet layout fixes…") sorts first in newest-first order. The PRD reads AC1 as "title tier first", which the code meets. The operator's own examples "eltmon"/"personal site" still do not match conversation 2832 by design (D9; "eltmon" is not in its title).
